objective.name: sandbox.dsl.parallel.remote.error
objective.description: Run one successful remote branch and one failing remote branch in parallel and close fail-closed.

#root.role: Launch one successful remote wrapper call and one failing remote matter read concurrently, then terminate with one propagated error response.

effects.terminal_error: The composite flow closes with one propagated terminal error.

transformation_contract.morphing: A local DSL request becomes one terminal propagated error after concurrent remote success and failure branches are evaluated together.
invariants: One remote wrapper branch is expected to succeed while one remote matter.read branch is expected to fail.
The parallel flow stays fail-closed and emits a single terminal error instead of exposing partial success payloads.
success: This scenario has no nominal success payload contract because its intended observable result is a propagated terminal error.
If all branches unexpectedly succeed, the test fixture would no longer represent the intended fail-closed composition case.
failure: The terminal response fails with a structured error when the remote matter.read branch cannot resolve the requested matter.
Only one terminal error response is emitted even though another parallel branch may have succeeded.
notes: This scenario exists to prove terminal closure semantics for >parallel in the presence of one remote branch failure.
The successful remote branch is part of the setup and should not leak its payload as a second terminal response.
